reason: Paragraph says the king 'is destined for rotundity, i.e., wholeness, but is prevented from achieving it by his original defect.' 'Destined for' is a passive teleological state, not active striving; the edge's relation overstates agency and drops the prevention. Quote accurate, claim_type correct.

Paragraph asserts 'the identification of the transformative substance with God' — with God, not with the God-image (imago Dei). Substituting the Jungian technical node god-image is a conceptual shift Jung does not make in this paragraph; the identification is Ripley's ('a bold stroke for a canon'), so the source should be named. Claim_type jung-reports-parallel is correct.
Paragraph: Ripley 'identify[ies] the king with the Ancient of Days from Daniel 7:9.' Direction correct, quote exact, jung-reports-parallel with source Ripley/Cantilena is right.

Paragraph: peacock flesh 'was just the right food for the mother in her attempt to rejuvenate the old king and to give him immortality.' Queen Mother -> renews -> king; direction correct. Jung asserting the Cantilena's symbolic action; quote accurate.
Paragraph: the queen is 'a tutelary madonna who adopts the king as her son.' Direction correct (queen adopts king, not the reverse); quote exact; jung-asserts fits Jung's interpretive statement.
Paragraph: 'In alchemy, the end of the work announced by the cauda pavonis was the birth of the filius regius.' The peacock's tail heralds the birth of the King's Son; direction and quote correct.

Paragraph: 'For seventeen hundred years... the lapis was brought into more or less clear connection with the ancient idea of the Anthropos,' asserted in Jung's own scholarly voice ('as I have shown in Psychology and Alchemy'). Corresponds-to is a fair rendering of 'connection'; quote accurate.

Paragraph: Khunrath's inscription calls the peacock 'bird of Hermes' and 'blessed greenness,' 'both of which symbolize the Holy Ghost or the Ruach Elohim.' Reported designation per Khunrath; jung-reports-parallel with source Khunrath is exactly right; quote accurate.

The sentence is 'The peacock is an ancient Christian symbol of resurrection, like the phoenix' — the subject is the peacock as bird in Christian tradition, not the cauda pavonis (tail-display stage of the opus), and the object is resurrection specifically. Attaching the Christian resurrection symbolism to the alchemical stage-node conflates two entities Jung keeps distinct in this passage.

Paragraph: the phoenix 'plays a considerable role in alchemy as a symbol of renewal and resurrection, and more especially as a synonym for the lapis.' Reported alchemical designation; jung-reports-parallel correct; quote accurate.

Paragraph: 'Blood is one of the best-known synonyms for the aqua permanens.' Stated flatly in Jung's own voice about alchemical usage; quote accurate; direction trivially correct for a synonym relation.
Paragraph: the alchemists 'assert that the prima materia and the vessel were identical.' Jung reports the alchemists' assertion; jung-reports-parallel is the correct claim_type; quote accurate.

Direct quotation from the Introitus apertus: 'the green lion, I say, who in truth is the Babylonish dragon, who kills all with his venom.' jung-quotes-source with source Introitus apertus is exactly right; quote verbatim. Minor note: the source specifies the Babylonish dragon, so the object node could carry that qualifier, but the identity claim is the source's own.

Paragraph: 'In general, Venus appears as the feminine aspect of the king, or as we should say, his anima.' Jung's own translation into psychological terms; jung-asserts correct; quote accurate. (Strictly it is the king's anima, worth noting on the edge.)
Paragraph: 'The prima materia is called meretrix... The stone, the filius regius, is the son of this whore.' Direction correct (filius born of meretrix); quote accurate.

Paragraph: 'over and above that he represents a dominant of consciousness, such as a generally accepted principle or a collective conviction or a traditional view.' Jung's core psychological interpretation of the Rex; jung-asserts correct; quote accurate.

Paragraph says the queen's 'consciousness is enriched by a knowledge of the collective unconscious' during her pregnancy. Being enriched by knowledge of the collective unconscious is not assimilating the collective unconscious itself — that phrasing overreaches into a wholesale absorption Jung does not claim (what is assimilated, per §424, are products of the anima).

Paragraph: the queen-lion uroboric exchange 'is explained by what we would consider an offensive identification of the queen with the mother of God.' Jung reports the Cantilena's implicit identification; jung-reports-parallel correct (source could usefully be tagged Ripley, Cantilena); quote accurate.

Paragraph: 'the smell of flowers attests that the rebirth of the king is a gift of the Holy Ghost or of Sapientia, thanks to whom the regeneration process could take place.' Direction correct (rex renewed-by Holy Ghost, not the reverse); quote accurate; jung-asserts acceptable for Jung's own interpretive statement about alchemical symbolism.

Paragraph: Luna joins Sol, 'initiating the second and usually final stage, the rubedo. With that the work is completed, and the lapis... has taken shape.' The rubedo culminates in the lapis; 'produces' is a fair rendering. Ellipsis omits only the description of the lapis ('a living being endowed with soul and spirit and an incorruptible body') and is not misleading.

Paragraph: Luna 'carries the king in her body as her adopted son. This gives the king immortality in a divine and incorruptible body' — i.e., the corpus glorificationis (echoed in §435: 'resurrection in a glorified body'). Direction correct; quote accurate.

Paragraph: 'As the square represents the quaternio of mutually hostile elements, the circle indicates their reduction to unity. The One born of the Four is the Quinta Essentia.' Quintessence produced from the four elements; direction correct; quote accurate.
